about: Short contextual tips (conventions.md §15). Each tip: id, context, en (≤140 chars), optional command. English only: skills translate a tip into the user's language when they show it. dev_state.py tip <context> returns the least-shown one, each at most twice (autonomy.tips: on | off | always).

tips.en: Standard issues wait in the queue and enter the next milestone's buffer (20%). See the queue with /dev-kit:backlog.
Small, low-risk items are handled in the cool-down between a gate and the next milestone (turn it on in the interview).
Hotfix: only for critical or high bugs in delivered work. One at a time; QA of that task only, then deploy and a patch version.
Bug in the milestone being built: it goes into that milestone now, like the fix tasks QA creates.
Scope changes go through PRD → review → replan and land in a future milestone; the cadence never changes.
More than 2 hotfixes in this milestone: if everything is urgent, nothing is. Reclassify what can wait as standard.
Each milestone takes queued issues up to its buffer (20%). The rest waits; milestones are never pushed or renumbered.
Gate passed. With cool-down on, small issues are fixed now, before the next milestone: autonomy.cooldown on.
Want to try the milestone yourself? A local preview can start after each approved gate (local_deploy in the interview).
Some findings were deferred. Promote the ones that matter to issues with /dev-kit:issue --from <F-id> <scope>.
Found a bug or want an improvement? Just describe it: /dev-kit:issue "what happens". The kit classifies it for you.
Classes: expedite = hotfix now · current = this milestone · standard = next buffer · intangible = cool-down · change = replan.
Prefer a picture? /dev-kit:board opens a live Scrum board (kanban, burndown, impediments) in your browser.
Curious how much each stage cost? /dev-kit:costs shows tokens and estimated US$ per stage.
/dev-kit:feedback grades each stage of the session and suggests improvements to the kit.
/dev-kit:backlog lists everything pending: issues, tasks, parked questions, deferred findings and deploys.
To let autopilot run overnight: autonomy level unattended plus a permission allowlist (/fewer-permission-prompts).
Hotfix tasks run before everything else, even with a pending gate. Only one hotfix is open at a time.
Between milestones autopilot pulls queued issues into the buffer and, with cool-down on, fixes small ones first.
Need your own prices? /dev-kit:costs --csv exports every token count; prices live in .dev/costs/prices.json.
The feedback report and export carry no project data; review them and send them to the dev-kit author if you like.
Lost? /dev-kit:help shows what to do next, how each skill works and short recipes for common tasks.
Not sure which skill to use? /dev-kit:help <question> answers with the right command.
